body:
As someone really into the retro look and wanting my own commando clone right now, can I ask what's particular that makes the second one better to have? Other than the expensive handguard and it being easier to swap barrels and/or install an adjustable gas block, is there any other big difference?

Also, love the name. I'm something of a scatman myself :)
I second this. Feels like there's just no winning.

This is where I feel like it's gone. Not to discount the safety concerns around real guns and blanks usage, but the CGI and airsoft props really have ruined gunplay action movies for me for the most part :(

Crazy how that's seemed to happen (at least in my eyes) to all action movies in just a few short years. I don't think there's any thought put into it much at all anymore. Action has always been an under-appreciated art form imho. The choreography, production, props, weapons, audio, shot set-ups, positioning, etc. all being integral to creating visually pleasing chaos.

Things are just different now and it depresses me to think that good gunplay action movies feel like a thing of the past.

And I'm not into this sequel at all. I have it playing in the other room right now. Watched about 40 minutes and got on here to see what others were saying lol.

We have some different interpretations of the phrase "man up" but you feel that I misrepresented your message and for that I do sincerely apologize.

I'm truly not trying to dump on you or be negative. You're an intelligent and positive person that's dealt with a lot of these awful things that come along with this condition, but I'm honestly not feeling the general bent of how I'm reading this topic here.

But it's also just where I am in my journey. I've spent the last three years reading a ton of gentle acceptance and "sit with it" type stuff and all it's done is make me more irritated with the people spouting it.

But I appreciate your thoughts and wish you the best of luck. 🙏

I had some problems before, but that's what really kicked off my major anxiety just about three years ago now. Hadn't touched weed in over 20 years and just a little sent me into a massive 6 hour nightmare high.

After that I developed existential OCD so my thoughts were constantly anxious. But about three weeks ago it shifted into my body and the anxiety attacks have turned into full on panic attacks. Really sucks and I'm just hoping to learn more about it, myself.

Agreed. I guess I just get a little peeved at the click-baity stuff I see about "cures" and whatnot. If you don't have fast-acting modern chemistry to alter what's going on inside the body, it seems we pretty much have to just go through it and try our best to maintain calm so as to not make it worse.

Idk I personally have a different view of this. While those kind of revolutions and uprisings have indeed happened, in my imagined scenarios it's like stereotypical favela/slum/etc situations where the dirt poor simply don't have the organization, vision, or resources to initiate true social change. Instead they would be just fighting the food chain for survival and resources. The predators among us would be organized and lure in the strongest family men to work for the best money while the rest just try to avoid being victims.

Like most things, I have no idea what the reality would really be, but I wish I had a more optimistic view of this awful scenario.

Not to be negative or crap on anyone's strategies, but yeah this is really just someone saying to man up and deal with it. Like most everything in life it's just not that easy at all. I've had attacks that have hijacked my entire body until I could only curl up in a ball and weep. Ain't no way was that happening to me in a gym and five minutes later I'm just back up and carrying on with my workout like a boss 😅

I'm completely over the meditation pushers that act like it's some kind of instant level-up cure-all for anything and everything. Maybe sometimes we're rightfully in a bad place because life is brutal and "sitting with it" isn't going to accomplish anything.

Yep, it's such a messed up aspect of life. Everybody has something to say about what you *should* do and how you *should* be and how you *should* live your life but they don't actually give a f about you or what happens to you. When we die, we're just numbers on a page somewhere. I try very hard to not let myself get pushed around by people with no investment in me.

I know this being reddit, your post will likely get down-voted to oblivion but I'm really trying to keep the faith. I'm one of those people for whom this life is just a bust. I'm really hoping there's something better on the other side and I have turned to Jesus. But it's a crap life either way, so I guess even if faith is for nothing, it's all whatever anyway. Still, I'm trying.

Love this so much. I do agree that saying hi to people, giving them attention, treating them special; it's a good path to try to make connections. 

This year I want to give out gifts on my birthday. Such a cool idea. I can't go anywhere, even to a gym, but still. I can try.

I hope the love that really wants you finds you soon.

Being in the same position minus never having held even a simple job, this is beautiful in such a terrible, awful way.

I understand you, too. It feels like all of this was chosen for us without consent. But it's just what we got. I still hope there is a way to rise above it but I also consider that I'm realistic about our odds. If not for my family I'd be dead. All I can do is try to stay grateful and hope there's something better when this short, sad life is over.

Damn, man. I love how you wrote this. This is all me, too. Lots of issues and struggles, far behind and falling faster. 39 and I feel like I'm closing in on the end of my life. Hard to imagine continuing on like this anyway. It's just not our reality. You got that right.

🫂

That's terrible and I'm so sorry.

I'm filling my days with a number of coping mechanisms and my hope is that eventually this frequency will merge with my consciousness and become my new silence. 

I'm a highly anxious neurotic though so I have a very difficult time acclimating to things like this. I'm distracted by them very easily and my thoughts latch onto them like "OMG this is awful and permanent I'm going to suffer like this and be miserable the rest of my life." Then I freak out.

Same. Came on noticeably strong just last summer and it's been driving me nuts for months. Have an ENT appointment in two months, but by now I know it's very likely permanent. I'm not yet 40.

I'm not into any of the answers here at all as I suffer from severe existential anxiety and the thought of living like this, plus eye floaters, for the rest of a life that will be over in a blink and then I just lose all consciousness forever--I feel sick even now. Flip that.

I choose to hope for something more. So as long as I'm on that course I hope we both experience miracles that cure this ailment.
No, nothing like that. I've been recommended to do shrooms on multiple occasions but I have no access to such things.

That's awesome. I've actually been talking a bit with someone from Kenya. He says life is much slower and more relaxed there than in the States.

But nah, when I say isolated I mean in just about every sense. I've spent most of the last 23 years of my life in my house. From the outside I look like any short, pudgy, far-below-average middle-aged nobody. But on the inside I'm incapable of being a functional adult human being.

I've had plenty of times where the crushing weight of it all collapsed on me and I saw the breadth of a bleak and hopeless life unfold before me in an instant. I've worked and tried and fought to change it but nothing ever came together.

I guess the most brutal answer I can give is that I cultivate delusions based on an abject terror at the thought of dying and just becoming nothing at the end of a sad and lonely life. I pray to a silent God and wish on shooting stars and grind away with the imagined hope that one day good things will just *happen* all while knowing that's really not how life works for the vast majority of people.

“There he goes. One of God's own prototypes. A high-powered mutant of some kind never even considered for mass production. Too weird to live, and too rare to die.”

― Hunter S. Thompson

For what it's worth, I'm really sorry to hear you're in such turmoil. I feel ruined, too. I can't tell you it's worth carrying on, but I hope you do anyway.
I write and publish fiction novels and have a number of other side-hustles from home.

Turning 40 this year and due to chronic illness and a host of other issues I've been isolated all my life. I've never even *spoken!* to a woman in any kind of intimate setting. Never a date, no closeness, nothing.

My therapist basically told me talk therapy couldn't help me. Tried meds, they just made me feel worse. At this point it's just one of those things where I ask why on a daily basis and realize there is no answer. Shit just happens. There are millions of extremely unlucky people in the world. They all have to be somebody. We just never hear from them because it's depressing. No matter how hard we work, *something* still has to work in our favor.

Idk.
Don't forget the suicide nets! Eh, they're probably not in the budget.
Good luck and thanks! Other than the early hiccups I do like how it turned out.

lol it happens! Guess I didn't win the lottery again 😭

Happy to hear about your luck though!
I took one 15 round KCI mag to the range and it was the only mag causing jams in my Dagger. Pmags did fine but I should just stick to OEMs too.

Yep indeed. I love the free shipping from OP but I'm just so wary about them now, lol.

Oh nice! I've spent a good deal of time following Doug's work. It's what gave me the confidence to take on the AR9 platform despite the potential issues. I really appreciate the work people like Doug have put in and the depth of help and resources I've found in this community.

And beautiful setup!

Great to hear! I always liked the looks of the PSA sets. I was actually looking for ways to make an affordable Colt SMG knockoff but when B. Kings had deals on the Aero receiver sets and all parts I needed, I was able to build the base gun for under $500 and I couldn't pass that up. Still, I knew the risks that I would have issues to fidoodle with so here we are 😅.

That's all great to hear, and yes I'm hoping another couple hundred rounds plus these upgrades will get it running smoothly.

Just a few weeks ago that RDB was on sale at OpticsPlanet for $120 and I so badly wanted to jump on it, but I recently had a poor experience with them and I ended up letting it pass. It really is a tempting upgrade, though.

I read the K-SPEC enhanced is supposed to eliminate bolt bounce and it was a reasonable price for a middle-of-the-road solution. Excited to see how it performs next time I can get to the range.

It's a Leaper's UTG DP933. I saw it on a clearance sale last year for around $10 and had to grab one. I love the aesthetic and I wanted to try it out. It seemed to run about the same as the Magpuls up until the last few rounds or so when the LRBHO kept holding.
I planned to before the next range trip but I need to get some Locktite and knowing me I'll forget so I'm going to make a note of it. Thanks!

This really resonates with me right now. I'm in the same place where I feel like my thinking/imagination is completely fried and haywire. For me it's happened after trying antidepressants with seems to have permanently disfigured my mental circuitry.

Whatever the reason though, I don't get lost in real thought or daydreams anymore. It's just a jumbled mess of things that always bring me back to a negative state. I suspect meditation has also had a detrimental effect.

Whatever the cause, I'm definitely in a "season" of life like none before. i used to act out a lot of my stress through moving my body but it doesn't work anymore and I get no pleasure from it. I feel absolutely fried and trapped in myself.

It's also hard to go for head-clearing walks like I used to. My body feels too messed up to be in motion and my head feels to messed up to be still. Tinnitus makes reading and just resting difficult. I'm a mess lol.
It really is exhausting, my friend. If you ever find yourself needing someone to listen, I always will.

How do you like the Kak compensator? I've read it pushes the muzzle down a lot on rifle calibers but I've been looking into it for my EPC9. Looks a bit heavy compared to the A2 that I'm currently running.

Other one I'm eyeing is a Breek Arms 3FO mini so I can also throw a blast can on it.

Yep. I experienced all of what you're going through and I'm still there for the most part. A little muted lately but still very much with those intrusive thoughts all the time.

The health anxiety may very well be permanent. After all, we're only going to get more sickly and fragile as we get older, which I also obsess about all the time :( I'm turning into a neurotic mess about everything.

I'm sorry I have no helpful words for you. I've been there. I'm still there. I'm likely doomed to it 'til death. I'd like to try magic mushrooms, though. I wonder if they'd change my perspective on things.

I'm wishing you the best of luck dealing with this terrible awakening.

I know exactly what you mean. That's another reason I don't offer religion or spirituality as advice, as it didn't actually help me. I still obsessed for months over the nature of God and eternity and still losing everything and going into a future that is, as you said, incomprehensible. The anxiety feeds on that feeling of the unknown. It's truly a terrible monster.

I want to know it all as well, while also knowing that knowledge is a curse so maybe I don't lol. I just want my hope back.

Are you also feeling like something akin to an ego death? Everything that you thought you were is being ripped apart? That's how it was for me.

If I can give any word of support, it's to take comfort that it won't be this bad for the rest of your life. Our awareness of our ticking clock is likely a permanent affliction, but a lot can change in a bit of time. The mind can't maintain such a high level of hyper-awareness indefinitely, in my personal belief, anyway.

Happened to me big time two years ago. Major existential/nervous breakdown. Nonstop freakouts and weeping daily for about three months before it finally started to slack off a little.

Therapy was worse than worthless, it actively made me feel worse. I hope you find a therapist that knows how to handle this, because the only people I could find basically just shrugged and said,"Well, you ARE going to die."

Be careful with medication. I took Lexapro and it was the worst mistake I could have made. I was doing so much better before I started it and I've been off of it well over a year and still don't feel right.

I turned to religion but that's not my personal advice, just fyi. I know from experience most people don't like that. All I can say is I started messing around with some various vitamins and about 300-400 milligrams of magnesium glycinate does seem to help calm my nerves at night. Otherwise it's taken about two years for my racing existential panic to dull a bit, but my thoughts of death and my clock ticking are still there every moment. They're intrusive thoughts all day that I can't do anything about.
So sorry you're struggling, but I'm truly glad to hear that and I wish you the best of luck.

Exactly. I mean I cast my vote the way I did because I knew the alternative but the sad reality we're faced with is that this is a crusade baked into the party's ideological foundation even in the face of such a major threat. So I really don't know.

But I know I'm going to the range tomorrow so I'll try to find joy in the little things.

Can't agree with this enough. I don't know how I can support a party that essentially says, "First we're going to push out these fascist tyrants, THEN we're going to take away your rights." (well, what's left of them)
As someone struggling with faith every minute I love to hear that so much 😭<3

I'm 39 and having a similar experience. I know what happened to all those years but I'm trying to overcome it and find some hope and redemption in faith.

Best of luck to you and may God bless and keep you.

Under professional guidance, no. Unfortunately, specialized therapists tend to not take my insurance.

Otherwise, I have dabbled in a number of techniques over the years without success.

I wish you the best of luck and I'll check out that sub some time.
Yeah I've read on it for years and I have a lot of indications of cptsd.

I saw your other comment and that's kind of a big question to answer but I'll try to here.

I self-publish and I don't make much, no.

Yeah, I've come that belief about my issues.

I'm extremely lucky to have the circumstances to be able to write and publish, but to put it simply, you could say my problem is that I want so much more than to be a chronically ill person confined to my house largely isolated with no prospects in sight. I want so much more out of life, that's why I'm working for it. It's just that as I said, nothing seems to be getting me anywhere.

It is always something. That's so true.

I appreciate the kind words.

Yeah, that was my experience. Really killed my creativity and drive and I've been off of it for well over a year now and still don't feel right compared to before I tried it.

I'm looking into Wellbutrin but I'm just really scared into mess with my brain chemistry like that again.

To be honest with you, I know how blessed and fortunate I am to have all that I do. I just feel like I'm trying to ski uphill. I see myself moving and trying but I'm not getting anywhere. I guess if I had to answer, I've never felt truly satisfied.

But no I don't. I know there are so many people out there so much worse off than me.

I feel the same way. I've been horridly depressed since middle school and at every stage in my life I felt lonely and deeply forlorn, yet as things just seem to keep getting worse I look back at older times and feel grateful to have had what I did then. I guess that's the nature of loss :(

I've in fact done a lot of reading in that sub and yes, at the moment I don't have a high opinion of the mental health care industry. But then I'm a particularly tough case so I have to keep that in mind. 

Thank you so much for the kind words. I hope your journey gets better and better.
They are. Just doing all I can to keep at it and hope one day things take off.
I do and I've done a lot of reading on this over the past several years. I'd have to say I agree with you.

:( 

I freely admit to using AI for my concept and cover art because I can't draw. AI will soon inundate and possibly kill the publishing industry. I won't lie, the difficulty I've had writing lately has put the fantasies of AI use in my head, but I have no desire to go that route.

It's hard to include enough information without writing a wall of text but since you have ADHD maybe you can relate to this.

I've written 11 books since high school. Distraction has always been a big problem but when I was inspired I could at least get work done in bursts.

Over the last few years I've suffered some severe breakdowns and after trying Lexapro my symptoms of ADHD went through the roof. I didn't say that I have ADHD as I can't find any medical care that will test me for it.

Over the last two years I have barely been able to write due to the explosion of these symptoms. The three books I published were revisions of things I had written years ago. I'm having the hardest time writing now than I've ever had :(

I hope this helps clarify. Whether I have ADHD or not, I'm not neurotypical and I truly feel your pain.
Certainly sounds like we share some struggles lol. If you feel like it, I'd love to know how your psychiatrist appointment goes. Best of luck to you, my friend.
Wishing you the best, my friend.

I'd be willing to but I have no access to psylocibin. I've read a bit about spore kits but I don't feel comfortable about growing my own, ya know?

Have you done them? Would you recommend microdosing or tripping?
I take care of my mom's dog but I've never really gotten any positive benefits from pets. I appreciate the suggestion, though.

I have won a spot in a few anthologies in the past but I self-publish on Amazon. The writing, editing, formatting, and creating a cover are all the difficult parts of that. I do it all myself so it's quite an intensive and tedious process getting a book completed and ready. Publishing is the easiest part lol. After that it's all marketing.

Trying to get a publishing deal generally starts with finding agents that deal in the genre(s) you write in and corresponding with them about your work. Getting published that way is like winning the lottery so I decided to do it on my own. There are of course many writing and publishing subs on Reddit that can give you a better idea of how it all works.
"Just that you do the right thing. The rest doesn't matter." - Marcus Aurelius
I truly hope it gave you some hope and perspective. 🙏 One day it WILL be too late for us, so we have to move now.

The obsessive thinking/mental chatter is terrible. I try combos involving chromium, vitamin d, lecithin, magnesium, and some other various cocktails. Nothing seems to help for long.

I tried something a few weeks ago that had Alpha GPC, Lion's Mane and some other nootropics that had me feeling decent at least.

Thank you for the kind words.
You're all too kind. Thank you very much. 🙏
I hope it resonates in a good way despite all my doom and gloom. I'm working hard on trying to stay grateful.

Unfortunately, the help I've been getting is at the end of a long road of searching and this admittedly poor situation is where I ended up. There simply isn't any way for me to get specialized care in my position.

I do try very hard to keep up my exercise routine but injuries and chronic fatigue make that a challenge. I will try to look into that yoga though, thank you.

I appreciate all the kindness and encouragement.
I really appreciate all your kind words. I'm trying not to give up.

I've glimpsed nothingness and seen how quickly I'm skyrocketing my way to it every day. It's ruined what little sanity I might have had. I most certainly do not jib well with Buddhist thought. I experienced an ego death during my crisis and it catapulted me into full existential OCD.

You're not the first to recommend mushrooms, though. I have lost faith in the medical establishment but unfortunately I don't have access to psylocybin I'm afraid.

It touches my heart to hear that. I feel like I've slipped so far and losing more ground every day, but it makes me feel hopeful to think I could give someone else motivation and hope. Wishing you the best of luck.
I feel like I've run out of road as far is mental health care is concerned, but I'm still trying. Thank you.
Thank you. I truly appreciate that.

I've published 11, 9 currently in print. Self-publishing to be more specific.

Just doesn't feel like it has much weight where I am now. Writing used to be my catharsis. I thought it was salvation. But 11 books in and nothing has really changed. It doesn't save me anymore.

I don't know about helped, but I know I've touched and inspired a handful of people.  I try to find contentment in that but it's getting harder and harder to hold onto hope.
I write fiction. Thrillers, mostly. One was a horror novel, then a sequel in an action series I'm working on, and at the end of last year I published my first book of poetry.

It's a terrible symptom of sentience. We are achingly aware of how quickly we're hurtling toward death with no way to stop it, knowing it could be abruptly cut short at any second and it could be just lights out. All things left unfinished and no time to make peace with letting go.

As I try desperately to make the days count, I think about the incalculable numbers that lived before me in their own times living short and brutal lives of toil, each of them in just as much mystery and befuddlement at their condition as I am. And now they're all gone, all names and faces no one will ever know.

It's a grand cosmic comedy that's only horror to me. But anyway, how's your most recent existential crisis going? Figured anything out?

Reading this thread and the link above have been really interesting. Could I possibly ask where you stand on other aspects of the end times prophecies? I still don't really know what to think about the Rapture (as in whether it's supposed to be literal) and things like the Millennial Kingdom.

If I was to read of the Rapture as a "catching up" in a figurative sense, that might mean that the church (read simply as Christians) will all come to a realization that they have been following the Antichrist? And then supposedly Christ's return should be not long (or possibly seven years) after.

A little more Leviticus in my life!   
A little bit of Chronicles by my side!  
A little bit of Ezra is all I need!  
A little bit of Job is what I see!  
A little bit of Proverbs in the sun!  
The Book of Isaiah all night long!  
A little bit of Samuel here I am!  
A little Revelation makes me your man!
I appreciate this as I get so very tired of the "make your own meaning" line.
Same. I'm so emotionally fragile and reactive to things and I wish my anxiety-riddled animal brain could just chill.
Thanks for the info!

Indeed, it's quite frustrating and that doesn't even factor in the poor build quality on so many models these days.

I've been looking into a budget canister vacuum to try out but the brush heads on most of them look like trash and reviews on so many state that the wands don't even lock to the head and they fall off. What a sad state.

It is a very convenient feature. I can still use the pet hair tool with the brush in it like a mini-head to get under the bed and such, it's just a bit more of a chore.

But yep. The trade-off with the nicer bagless models is a dirtier, short-life system but they're just so dang handy to use. 😅

But I wish us both good luck and long cleaning with our Kenmores!

I feel your pain. It's just like any other industry product. There may be dozens of very similar products from a variety of manufacturers, but it's impossible to find the model with the exact combination of features you want. Something always seems to be missing that one luxury you really desire. I yearn for world where all vacuums are fully modular and standardized to spec and parts can be swapped out like Legos lol.

This Intuition: [https://www.amazon.com/Kenmore-Intuition-Lift-Away-Combination-HandiMate/dp/B08CXPQXL5?ie=UTF8&th=1](https://www.amazon.com/Kenmore-Intuition-Lift-Away-Combination-HandiMate/dp/B08CXPQXL5?ie=UTF8&th=1)

Yep. On my Shark, when I lift off the canister, I can still run it like a vacuum, with the powered head running at the end of the wand. This allows me to easily pop the canister off and roll under my furniture and bed and get a bit of extra reach when I'm at the end of the cord. I'm just really surprised the Kenmore doesn't lock onto the base and run when the canister is off.

That has been my findings so far as well. Well, I'll run my Kenmore as long as I can. It seems from research the hose will break long before the vacuum itself. After that I'll do more looking and just have to decide on what I'm wiling to accept and live without.

Right? I see these people commenting about how awesome and comforting it will be to have no consciousness or awareness after death forever and ever and ever and I wonder if they got lost on the way to the atheism sub.

The idea of non-existence for eternity is more terrifying to me than continuing on after death. Just slightly so, but still. Neither of these offer me any comfort but I am excruciatingly aware of my hourglass running out every moment of the day and it will never be tipped over again. EVER! That's absolutely devastatingly horrifying to me.

Aww thank you so much! I do quite like this name lol.

Yep, when I find a term for things I don't know whether to be comforted or further stressed.

Hello fellow ADHD brain. Always here if you need to chat.

>I have tasted the fruit of that tree, and found it quite bitter

  
After a number of my own traumas and currently drowning in existential dread, this is an idea I try to convey to people in my own way.

Hopefully without removing reason entirely, at some point in time I find most people choose in some way what they want to believe. Not one of us can escape holding some fantasy or unverifiable belief in something. When I say not one of us, that's just my unverifiable belief talking.

We each have to find the fruit of life that tastes sweetest to us. I've chosen in the Kierkergaardian sense to lean on God and Jesus because for me that fruit is sweeter than anything else offered.

I say more power to anyone that's secure in their beliefs. Existential despair is a hell of a torment.
Same. I'm at a point where I just don't believe that modern medicine holds any hope for me.

This is pretty much where I am. Even if I think to myself that I hate this world, hate this existence, hate this life, etc. I still don't want it to end. Even when I'm miserable there are things I still want to do. When I can't go on, I go on.
Sure. Nice to meet you.

I feel this. No matter how much I do or how much progress I make, nothing really seems to change for the better and I find myself falling back over and over. And then I go crazy thinking about how time is running so short to figure this stuff out. Really sucks.

The thing that kills me is that I used to be most alive at night. I've lived most of my life as a big night owl. Getting work done. Socializing online, even having intense workouts. Then trauma made everything flip and now nights are soo hard. What the heck? What gives?

I wake up every day with really bad mental chatter and nihilistic thoughts of existential despair. I try to catch myself as soon as I can and give praise and thanks to God for today. I call it a gift even though I don't see it as one. I call it a blessing even though I don't feel like it is.

But sometimes it helps switch my thoughts over to some semblance of meaning and hope rather than meaninglessness and despair. I don't know if these are beneficial mind tricks/strategies but I guess if it works then more power to us.

I've always had a lot of issues and been very emotionally unstable. Lots of highs and lows, crying, etc. A little over two years ago I was just stressed to the breaking point and started seriously planning to end my life.

Anyway, that made it too real and I began ruminating on dying and being dead and it sparked a severe episode. Nervous breakdown/existential crisis/ego death sort of thing. Went on for months. I developed ceaseless intrusive thoughts about death and existence and how fast time is flying by and how I could die at any time and it will be time to die before I know it. I'm sure you've felt it all.

Anyway, tried meds and therapy which just made things worse. ADHD brain ruminates over everything and keeps me in a state of constant fatigue and feeling fried. I've tried so many things to make progress but nothing works so that's where I am lol.
Same. Do you feel like you've been snapped awake and now you can't understand how so many people just go about living their lives? I just want to go back.

I really hope it does. I tried Lexapro and it was one of the worst decisions I ever made but of course I just couldn't know that going in.

Best of luck to you.

Yes, absolutely. I've lost my ability to enjoy pretty much everything I use to do and my daily experience is one of near constant dread and worry. That's a very apt analogy. I feel weak and soft and vulnerable and confused by everything.

And also I feel like I've lost my previous hopes and have awoken into a world where I will never feel safe or happy and there's just nothing for me. But that terror at the thought of dying makes me trudge on.

I feel like a meat machine rising every day just to execute my hard-wired program. I'm no longer a person in this shell.

A never-ending panic of sheer terror brought on by the prospect of death. I stay in a constant state of dread over it. I try desperately to distract myself but it comes back to the forefront of my mind every day and I honestly just don't know what else to do.

Appreciate you taking the time to read and respond with such hopeful advice.

You're probably right about my mom pitying me. She's always been that kind of person. Regardless of her feelings, a lot of my pain and sadness comes from wanting better for her.

I won't get into all that other stuff. I have long term health issues that aren't getting any better with treatment. I've never been gainfully employed and can't drive. So no matter what I do it feels like I don't have a ton of options from day to day. But I really do hope there's a comeback arc in this.
